page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, resulting in 8 vCPUs. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and FMA instructions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory operations, contrasted with weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 1310.19, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6971.17 and a PassMark CPU score of 8191.37. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 389.72 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 48.91 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and web serving throughput also align with mid-range expectations, demonstrating 6.4 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.29 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Given its average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-threaded execution, this instance is best suited for multi-threaded applications, general-purpose web serving, Redis caching layers, and moderate database operations. It is less optimal for single-core bound processing or heavy cryptographic and compression tasks.
